Transportation Planning
The State Highway Plan
Presently Wisconsin's highway planning and development is a coordinated effort, statewide, by all levels and agencies of government. One major comprehensive effort that provides a foundation for coordinated highway development has been the State Highway Plan (figure 5). This plan, adopted by the State Highway Commission in 1966, seeks an optimal highway work for the year 1990. This is to be accomplished by upgrading the existing facilities to the necessary standards as well as adding new facilities as are needed to provide the necessary service. The Airport Spur route as called for in the plan is a major artieral connecting Interstate Route I-94 with General Mitchell Field, a major traffic generator.
Federal Directives
In September 1967, the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Transportation called for a program to help solve problems of access to major airports nationally. The Secretary requested coordinated efforts between the Federal Highway Administration and the Federal Aviation Administration in speeding up interstate travel nationwide and reducing the time spent on the ground by air travelers. Since that time, providing direct access between two types of interstate carriers has become a national goal.
